reviews.reason: The CIFs parse, symmetry-expand to full-occupancy Li4Nb2O2F10 (18 atoms; primitive Li2NbOF5), and share the strongly indexed C2 cell (39/39 selected lines), but the atomic realization is not established. Direct whole-profile tests of the instantiated CIFs give normalized residuals of about 0.217 and 0.245 versus about 0.067 when the same indexed reflections have free intensities; major lines near 28.04, 28.17, and 53.43 degrees have 10-16%-of-maximum integrated-intensity errors, far above the approximately 0.10-intensity baseline noise. The trace itself acknowledges substantial profile mismatch, derives coordinates through chemistry-penalized searches rather than a converged coordinate refinement, and identifies a near-degenerate alternative Li minimum that is not represented: both submitted CIFs have exactly the same Li site despite the final claim that this ambiguity was covered. Both also contain a full-occupancy 1.80 angstrom Li-Li periodic contact. Thus the cell is solved, but ordering/coordinates and periodic chemistry remain dubious enough that another attempt can materially improve or replace the submitted realizations.

reviews.proposed_branch: Instantiate and refine the trace's non-equivalent octahedral candidate D (OCTA seed 2101) in the established primitive P1 cell.
reviews.reason: The primary CIF is valid: it is an ordered, full-occupancy primitive P1 Z=1 cell with 9 atoms and composition Li2NbOF5; all 57 observed peaks of prominence >=1 are indexed within 0.024 degrees, its instantiated whole-profile Rwp is 0.0870 versus a free-intensity floor of 0.0816, and independent checks recover chemically consistent Li(+1), Nb(+5), O(-2), and F(-1) valences with a complete NbO1F5 octahedron and no overlap. However, the trace itself contains a concrete surviving realization that is absent from the submitted set: octahedral candidate D (seed 2101) was explicitly instantiated in the same primitive cell and composition, was found non-equivalent to both submitted A/C families by structure matching, and gave profile RMS 0.3144 (approximately Rwp 0.0905 from the reported data RMS 3.474), close to the selected model's 0.3024/0.0870 and the free floor 0.2833/0.0816. Its periodic shell is plausible (Nb-O 1.900 A, Nb-F 1.780-2.186 A, shortest contact Li-F 1.697 A, Li-Li 2.604 A), so chemistry does not veto it. It was neither relaxed to test convergence nor quantitatively rejected; therefore the exact ordering/coordinate ambiguity is not adequately covered, and another attempt is likely to add a materially different viable candidate.

The primary CIF is valid and primitive: it parses as ordered P1 with V = 102.1856 A^3, Z = 1, nine fully occupied sites, and composition Li2NbOF5; its charge assignment and complete periodic shells are chemically plausible (Nb has one O and five F neighbors at 1.600-2.323 A, with no overlap). Indexing is also strong (27/27 selected lines indexed, M(20) = 68.6, mean |delta 2theta| about 0.005 degrees). The decisive failure is atomic-coordinate evidence. The comparable-score report is unavailable, and the trace's auditable instantiated-CIF comparisons give full-profile RMSE values of 0.654, 0.667, and 0.693 intensity units for the three final CIFs, versus about 0.10 baseline noise; for the selected CIF this is approximately an 18% unweighted whole-profile residual and 6.6 times the noise. The models came from one Li2NbF6-prototype-seeded, flexible P1 rotation/distortion search, with parent Li coordinates restored after overfitting; there is no independent map/search convergence, Pawley lower-bound comparison, or quantitative support that distinguishes the submitted tilt/O-order variants. Thus the lattice and chemistry are established, but no submitted ordered atomic realization is sufficiently established for exact recovery, and another solution attempt is likely to add a materially different viable coordinate/order model.
